title: Virata: the year in disguise
hook: the forest years are over, and Yudhishthira asks each brother and Draupadi a plain question: what will you be?
carry: every disguise is built from something real

segments.voice: Yesterday the Yaksha's questions came to an end, and the voice at the lake showed itself as Dharma. Your line was the one who keeps the family fair. Like Yudhishthira choosing Nakula, did you think first of the side with no one speaking for it? Day eight hundred seven.

The forest is behind them now, and a harder stretch of the exile is ahead. The terms of the dice game were plain: one last year lived among people, without being recognized. If anyone sees through them, the exile begins again. So the five brothers and Draupadi sit together, and Yudhishthira asks each of them a question. Not where will you hide. What will you be? Where will you work, and as whom? They have chosen a kingdom to vanish into: the land of the Matsyas, ruled by King Virata. Today the Virata book opens with something close to a job interview, held in secret.
screen: `ONE YEAR, UNRECOGNIZED.` → `WHAT WILL YOU BE?` → `THE COURT OF KING VIRATA.`

segments.voice: Listen to the answers, because each one tells you something. Yudhishthira goes first. He will be Kanka, a Brahmin who plays dice with the king and keeps him company. Stop on that. The man whose love of dice cost them everything chooses dice as his cover. Bhima will be Vallava, the cook, and he'll wrestle if the court wants a show. The brother with the famous appetite will run the kitchen. Arjuna has a harder problem: the scars a bowstring leaves on a warrior's arms. He'll hide them under bangles and live as Brihannala, a eunuch who teaches singing and dance to the women of the palace. Nakula will keep the king's horses. Sahadeva will keep the cattle. And Draupadi, a queen, will serve the queen as Sairandhri, a maid who dresses hair. Notice what none of them does. Nobody pretends to a skill they don't have. Every disguise is built from something real. The rank is hidden. The person isn't. Then their priest, Dhaumya, gives them advice for life in a king's house, and it reads like advice for a first week at any new job. Don't take a seat that might belong to someone else. Speak when you're asked. Don't show off, and don't gossip about the king's private affairs. Be useful, and be quiet about it. The great heroes of the epic are about to spend a year as staff.
screen: `EACH ONE ASKED: WHAT WILL YOU BE?` · `THE DICE MAN CHOOSES DICE` · `EVERY DISGUISE BUILT ON A REAL SKILL` · then, large: `DHAUMYA: HOW TO LIVE AT COURT`

segments.voice: Settle into your seat, and let your breathing find its own pace. Bring to mind the roles you play: at work, at home, among friends. Pick one. Breathing in, ask what that role asks of you. Breathing out, find the real skill underneath it: patience, a good ear, steady hands. Stay with that one skill for a few breaths, the way Bhima's cooking sat under the name Vallava. If you pray, you can offer that skill in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Virata. The king of the Matsyas, whose court will hide the Pandavas and Draupadi for their year in disguise.
Your line: every disguise is built from something real. Today, in one role you play, notice the real skill it rests on, the part no costume could fake. Day eight hundred seven.

screen: `DAY 807 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.`

howItsDone: The Virata book is read and retold as part of the Mahabharata, and the disguises the Pandavas choose (Kanka, Vallava, Brihannala, Sairandhri) are familiar names from retellings and performances of the epic.

match.prompt: who hid as whom? tap the pairs.
pairs: Yudhishthira, playing dice with the king

myth: the Pandavas chose disguises with no link to their real skills
every disguise rested on something real: dice, cooking, music, horses, cattle.
Arjuna hid his bowstring scars under bangles
he lived as Brihannala, teaching song and dance in the palace.
Dhaumya advised them to stand out at court
he advised the opposite: take no one's seat, speak when asked, don't show off.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. dice cost you your kingdom. now you need a disguise for a royal court. what do you choose?
options: a guard at the palace gate.
a Brahmin who plays dice with the king.
a hermit who stays outside the city.
fork.reveal: he becomes Kanka, the king's dice companion. the very game that ruined him becomes his cover.

original.note: the king of the Matsyas; his name titles this book of the epic, the Virata Parva.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Pandavas simply went into hiding.
what it means: each chose a working life built on a real skill, hiding rank but not the person.
what a scholar hears: some readers hear the Virata book as a book of reversals: a king as courtier, a warrior as dancer, a queen as maid.
recall: dark, in red, with a noose
waits for a lapse, then enters Nala

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Virata Parva (Pandava-pravesa), the Pandavas choose their disguises and Dhaumya's counsel on living in a king's household
